content.content:
The detail panel presents the value inside the Content section according to that value's content type. The section's label, its place in the fixed kind, content, rationale order, and the Kind and Rationale sections themselves are unchanged: only how the Content section's own value is rendered varies with its type.

For content.type "text", "ears" and "review-criteria", the value is presented as running prose: the body is shown as wrapped text with paragraph breaks preserved and no code framing.

For content.type "visual-spec", "json-schema", "test" and "rust", the value is presented as formatted code: the body is shown verbatim in a monospaced block with its line breaks and indentation preserved, marked with the content type as content.type spells it.

For any content.type value not named above, the value is presented as formatted raw content: the same verbatim monospaced block, marked with the content type as content.type spells it. No type is refused, hidden or forced into one of the named renderings, so a value added under a new type still displays.

When content.ref is a list of repo-relative paths rather than "inline", the Content section's value is the content type together with those paths, shown in the same monospaced block, because the body then lives in the referenced files and is not carried in the node. An empty value still leaves the Content section in place with its label, showing the content type alongside it.

The rendering is a function of content.type and content.ref alone: no per-type parser, highlight grammar or extra field is needed, so even a type this decision does not name receives a total, predictable rendering.
content.rationale: The three sections are fixed in number, label and order, but the bodies they carry do not share one form: this graph alone holds prose decisions and ears requirements beside review criteria and a JSON schema kept in a file, and content types are open by design. One rendering for all of them would either wrap code as prose or bury prose in monospace, so the panel would misrepresent what kind of thing it is showing. This node settles the one choice left open for the Content section once the section frame is fixed: the value's content type selects its rendering, prose for the narrative types, a verbatim monospaced block for the structured ones, and the same block for every type the mapping does not name, so the openness of content.type costs no content its display. Because the rule reads only content.type and content.ref, and handles the declared path form of ref by presenting the type and paths rather than a body the node does not carry, it introduces no per-type vocabulary, parser or field the recorded node structure lacks, and it leaves every section label and the fixed order exactly as the frame decision set them. Collapse behaviour, relationship sections and the roster of sections stay with the decisions that own them.
